title: Peakform duplicate push notification postmortem
brief: Write the postmortem for the duplicate push notification incident on 2026-09-21 at Peakform Fitness, tracked as INC-2874 and owned by the Messaging team. A weekly workout reminder campaign was meant to go out once to 1240000 users. A retry bug in the queue consumer re-sent each message six extra times, so users got the same notification seven times, 7440000 duplicates in total, over 38 minutes. Opt-outs from push jumped to 3.4 percent of recipients (42160 users) against a normal 0.2 percent, and the app store rating dropped from 4.6 to 4.3 over the following week. Give it a "Summary", then an annotated "Timeline" in Pacific time: 16:00 campaign released; 16:04 the first consumer timeouts begin and retries start; 16:09 social media complaints appear; 16:15 support pages the Messaging on-call; 16:22 on-call pauses the campaign sender; 16:38 queue purged and duplicates stop. A "Contributing factors" section in prose, saying the consumer treated a slow downstream acknowledgement as a failure and had no idempotency key, the campaign tool allows sends to the entire user base without a staged ramp, and the pause switch took 7 minutes to find because it was undocumented. A "Customer impact" paragraph. Then "Action items", each with an owner and due date: add idempotency keys to the push consumer, Daniel Okonkwo-Reyes, 2026-10-09; require staged ramps of 1, 10 and 100 percent for sends over 100000 users, Priya Venkatesan, 2026-10-23; document the sender pause switch in the on-call guide, Messaging on-call, 2026-09-28; send an apology notice and in-app note to affected users, Customer Care, 2026-09-24. Plain and honest, no blame on the engineer who merged the change.

edit.request: Correct the number of affected users to 1260000 and the total duplicates to 7560000, and mark the sender pause switch documentation action as done.
